== Overview ==
It was formerly the village shrine of {{ill|Takabeya|ja|高部屋村|ko|다카베야촌|qid=Q11672972}} in {{ill|Ōsumi district|ja|大住郡|pl|Powiat Ōsumi (Kanagawa)|zh|大住郡|qid=Q11432367}} with the same shrine name, and was also revered as the general tutelary shrine of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kasuya-shō}}<ref group="注">The place name Kasuya of Kasuya-shō still remains, but note that “Kami'''Kasu'''ya” and “Shimo'''Kasu'''ya” are written with different characters.</ref>, including this district.

Its founding date is unknown. It is listed in the '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}' as one of 13 seats in Sagami Province and was the general tutelary shrine of 127 villages in Ōsumi District. However, {{ill|Takamori Shrine|qid=Q0|lt=Takamori Shrine}} in Takamori, Isehara, is also considered one of the claim shrines for the Shikinaisha “Takabeya Shrine.” One reason is that this shrine is said to have been called “Takabeya Shrine” before the Meiji-era {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ca|Shinbutsu bunri|de|Shinbutsu-Bunri|es|Shinbutsu bunri|fa|شینبوتسو بونری|fi|Shinbutsu bunri|fr|Shinbutsu bunri|id|Shinbutsu bunri|it|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|ru|Симбуцу бунри|tr|Şinbutsu-bunri|zh|神佛分離|qid=Q1970535}}, and inscriptions reading “Takabeya Shrine” remain on timbers and on the back side of the stone monument beside its {{ill|Torii|ar|توري|az|Torii|bcl|Torii|bg|Тории|ca|Torii|cs|Torii|de|Torii|el|Τορίι|eo|Torijo|es|Torii|et|Torii|eu|Torii|fa|توریئی|fi|Torii|fr|Torii|he|טוריאי|hu|Torii|hy|Տորիի|id|Torii|it|Torii|ja|鳥居|jv|Torii|ko|도리이|lt|Torii|ms|Torii|nl|Torii|no|Torii|oc|Torii|pl|Torii|pt|Torii|ru|Тории|simple|Torii|sl|Tori|sq|Torii|sv|Torii|ta|தொரீ|th|โทริอิ|tr|Torii|uk|Торії|uz|Torii|vi|Torii|wuu|鳥居|zh|鳥居|qid=Q234731}}<ref>[http://w1.oroti.net/~takamori/htdocs/ Sagami no Kuni Takamori Shrine] (official website), history page.</ref>.

The shrine preserves three old gagaku masks used in rituals from the Kamakura period onward, and a plaque reading “Hachimangū” written in early Genroku by Etsuzan Dōsō, the 7th abbot of {{ill|Manpuku-ji|arz|مانبوكو جى|de|Mampuku-ji|es|Manpuku-ji|fr|Manpuku-ji|id|Manpuku-ji|it|Manpuku-ji|ja|萬福寺|my|မန်းပုခုဂျိ|pt|Mampuku-ji|ru|Мампуку-дзи|th|มัมปูกุจิ|zh|萬福寺 (宇治市)|qid=Q576318}} (Ōbaku-zan, Uji, Kyoto), a monk who came from Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, China. Gyōan and Gyōhaku, who donated the komainu in front of the main sanctuary, were also monks of the {{ill|Ōbaku|az|Obaku|bg|Обаку|ca|Obaku|de|Ōbaku-shū|es|Obaku|fr|Ōbaku|hu|Óbaku|it|Ōbaku-shū|ja|黄檗宗|no|Ōbaku|pl|Ōbaku|pt|Ōbaku|ru|Обаку|sh|Obaku|sr|Obaku|vi|Hoàng Bá tông|zh|黄檗宗|qid=Q384728}}, suggesting a period of strong ties with Ōbaku along with the former bettō temple Jingū-ji.

At present it is concurrently administered by {{ill|Isehara Daijingu|ja|伊勢原大神宮|qid=Q11378955}}, where one may also receive {{ill|Shuin|de|Shuin|fr|Goshuin|ja|朱印 (神社仏閣)|ko|슈인|ms|Syuin|simple|Shuin|zh|御朱印|qid=Q7504772|lt=seal stamps}}.

== Rituals ==
[[File:Takabeya-jinja(Isehara) Kaguraden.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Kagura hall]]
A ritual called “Shiokumi no Shinji” has been held in September for over 1,000 years since the {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|ceb|Panahon sa Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292}}. The beach sand used in the rite is taken from Terugasaki Coast, where {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|de|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|it|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|ja|住吉三神|mni|ꯁꯨꯃꯤꯌꯣꯁꯤ ꯁꯟꯖꯤꯟ|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနတ်သုံးပါး|pl|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|simple|Sumiyoshi sanjin|zh|住吉三神|qid=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi Ōkami}} (Ōsumi Daimyōjin) is said to have landed. میٹر|uz|Kilometr|vec|Chiłòmetro|vi|Kilômét|wa|Kilomete|war|Kilometro|wuu|千米|xmf|კილომეტრი|yi|קילאמעטער|zh|公里|zh_classical|公里|zh_min_nan|Kong-lí|zh_yue|千米|qid=Q828224|lt=km}} one way to Terugasaki to collect seawater, beach sand, and hondawara seaweed (sargassum). The seawater is used as fire-quelling sacred water; the beach sand is spread on the approach for purification; the hondawara is hung on shimenawa at the worship hall and torii.

== Precincts ==
Within the precincts are the main sanctuary, worship hall, {{ill|Kagura-den|es|Kaguraden|fi|Kaguraden|fr|Kagura-den|it|Kagura-den|ja|神楽殿|qid=Q94498}}, purification place, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=temizuya}}, {{ill|Bonshō|ar|بونشو|bn|বোনশো|de|Bonshō|es|Bonshō|fa|بونشو|fr|Bonshō|id|Bonshō|it|Bonshō|ja|梵鐘|ko|범종|pl|Japońskie dzwony, dzwonki i gongi|pt|Bonshō|ru|Бонсё|th|บนโช|zh|佛鐘|qid=Q8192099|lt=temple bell}}, playground equipment, and the following precinct shrines.

== National Registered Tangible Cultural Properties ==
; Main sanctuary
: Collapsed in the Great Kantō Earthquake and rebuilt in Shōwa 4. Most major timbers are reused from the pre-collapse main sanctuary rebuilt in {{ill|Shōhō|fa|شوهو|fr|Ère Shōhō|ja|正保|ko|쇼호|ru|Сёхо (Эдо)|simple|Shōhō|sr|Шохо|sv|Shōhō|tr|Shōhō|zh|正保|qid=Q1146192}} 4 (1647). Registered as a National Registered Tangible Cultural Property on February 25, 2016.
; Worship hall
: Rebuilt in Keiō 1 (1865). Like the main sanctuary, registered as a National Registered Tangible Cultural Property on February 25, 2016.

== Important Cultural Property of Kanagawa Prefecture ==
; Bell tower
: In {{ill|Shitoku|fa|شیتوکو|fr|Ère Shitoku|ja|至徳 (日本)|ko|시토쿠|ru|Ситоку|simple|Shitoku|sr|Шитоку|sv|Shitoku|tr|Shitoku|zh|至德 (日本)|qid=Q1146202|lt=Shitoku}} 3 (1386) December, Taira Hidenori donated a bronze bell. The bell is designated an Important Cultural Property of Kanagawa Prefecture.

== Access ==
* About 20 minutes on foot from {{ill|Isehara Station|arz|محطة ايسيهارا|fr|Gare d'Isehara|it|Stazione di Isehara|ja|伊勢原駅|ko|이세하라역|my|အိဆဲဟရဘူတာ|ru|Исэхара (станция)|ur|ایسہارا اسٹیشن|zh|伊勢原站|qid=Q4205219}} on the {{ill|Odakyū Odawara Line|de|Odakyū Odawara-Linie|es|Línea Odakyu Odawara|fa|خط اوداکیو-اوداوارا|fr|Ligne Odakyū Odawara|it|Linea Odakyū Odawara|ja|小田急小田原線|ko|오다큐 오다와라선|nl|Odawara-lijn|ru|Линия Одавара (Одакю)|th|รถไฟฟ้าโอดะกีวสายโอดาวาระ|zh|小田原線|qid=Q135176}}.
* Bus from the station north exit on {{ill|Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu|ja|神奈川中央交通|ko|가나가와 중앙 교통|qid=Q10854960}}:
** {{ill|I76 route|ja|神奈川中央交通伊勢原営業所|qid=Q11588882}} bound for {{ill|Aikō-Ishida Station|arz|محطة ايكو ايشيدا|it|Stazione di Aikō-Ishida|ja|愛甲石田駅|ko|아이코이시다역|my|အအိခိုး − အိရှိဒဘူတာ|ru|Аико-Исида|ur|آئی کو-ایشیڈا اسٹیشن|zh|爱甲石田站|qid=Q1107009}}, get off at “Kasuya-Kamijuku,” 3-minute walk.
** {{ill|I74 route|ja|神奈川中央交通伊勢原営業所|qid=Q11588882}} bound for Aiko-Ishida Station, get off at “Awakubo Iriguchi,” 4-minute walk.
